Caries

One randomized study measured salivary risk factors, and mapped deep-cavity trials measured sensitivity, vitality, or dentin formation. The records do not establish fewer new caries lesions.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One randomized study measured salivary risk factors, and mapped deep-cavity trials measured sensitivity, vitality, or dentin formation. The records do not establish fewer new caries lesions.

Summary of the Evidence

Four records are relevant: two in the exact “Caries” category (one 36-participant human randomized study of salivary caries-risk measures and one induced-caries rat experiment) plus two 2025 randomized studies mapped from deep-caries removal (27 teeth and 33 molars). The database does not flag overlap between the mapped reports. Those procedural studies assess adjunctive outcomes, not caries prevention.

Human and clinical evidence

The salivary-gland study reported improvement in bacterial and saliva risk markers. The deep-cavity studies reported lower postoperative sensitivity in one and greater mineralization of neoformed dentin in the other; neither demonstrates fewer caries lesions (Nemeth et al. 2019; Petta et al. 2025; de Santana et al., 2025). The records assess salivary risk markers, postoperative sensitivity, pulp vitality, or dentin formation rather than the incidence of new caries lesions. One mapped deep-caries report includes 27 teeth, not 27 independent patients, and studies adjunctive care after selective caries removal and restoration. A change in a salivary marker or short-term postoperative symptom cannot by itself establish fewer future cavities.

Primary original studies: Nemeth et al. 2019 Petta et al. 2025

Animal evidence

Laser alone did not reduce induced caries in rats. A modest advantage was reported when laser preceded fluoride (Müller et al., 2007).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Nemeth et al. compared polychromatic light spanning 480–3400 nm with LED wavelengths of 625, 660, and 850 nm, delivered 3 times weekly for 4 weeks. 625 and 660 nm are visible red; 850 nm is near-infrared. The study measured caries-risk factors, not incident caries. Deep-cavity reports use their own wavelength protocols and should not be pooled with prevention outcomes.

Interpretation

These studies support only limited conclusions about salivary markers and short-term restorative outcomes. A biomarker change is not equivalent to preventing future cavities. The mapped deep-caries studies concern an adjacent clinical setting and should remain distinguished from direct caries-prevention evidence.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low. Caries-risk markers and deep-cavity outcomes do not establish fewer caries lesions.
Publications and records4 unique titles, including 2 exact-category reports and 2 mapped deep-caries trials.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The human evidence concerns salivary caries-risk markers and adjunctive treatment after selective removal of deep caries, rather than prevention of new lesions. One rat study reports mixed findings. Changes in saliva, postoperative sensitivity, or dentin formation are surrogate or procedural outcomes and do not establish a reduction in caries incidence.
